posts.title: BYD H1 profit falls 20.5% as overseas growth fails to offset China weakness
posts.summary:
Overseas expansion lifted gross margin to 18.85%, but NEV weakness and foreign-exchange losses weighed on profit.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD reported a 20.54% decline in first-half net profit to 12.33 billion yuan, driven by domestic NEV market weakness and foreign-exchange losses.
Despite a 7.13% drop in total revenue, the company's gross margin improved to 18.85%, supported by strong growth in overseas markets.
Overseas sales surged 67.8% year-on-year, now accounting for approximately 44% of total sales, helping to offset the 15.72% decline in total NEV volume.
The company continues to prioritize R&D, with first-half investment reaching 28.9 billion yuan, more than double its net profit for the same period.

posts.title: FAW-VW opens ID. AURA T6 pre-sales, betting on locally developed smart tech to win over Chinese buyers
posts.summary:
The ID. AURA T6 starts at a pre-sales price of 135,900 yuan ($20,040) and offers a range of up to 660 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: FAW-Volkswagen has opened pre-sales for the ID. AURA T6, a mid-size SUV priced between 135,900 and 169,900 yuan.
The vehicle utilizes the CEA architecture co-developed with Xpeng, marking a strategic shift toward integrating local Chinese smart-driving technology.
High-end variants feature 192-channel LiDAR and a driver-assistance system powered by the Horizon Robotics Journey 6H chip, delivering 420 TOPS of computing power.
This launch represents Volkswagen's attempt to bridge the competitive gap with domestic Chinese EV brands by leveraging local supply chains for smart cockpit and autonomous driving features.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week in Review
posts.summary:
Hot Chips AI HW wave; HBM vs HBC; capacity buildout; Infineon's latest buy; advanced packaging enablers; foundry report; ASIC security threats; IC tariffs; executive changes; Nvidia, Synopsys earnings; dependence on Taiwan; wafer-scale 2D semiconductors.
The post Chip Industry Week in Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Hot Chips 2026 revealed major advancements in AI silicon, including IBM/Arm's 2nm dual-architecture processor and Microsoft's 3nm Maia 200 AI accelerator.
Memory bottlenecks remain a primary industry focus, with Nvidia introducing NVHBM and Qualcomm proposing High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) as an alternative to traditional HBM-plus-interposer designs.
Apple has transitioned to 2nm process technology for its M6 and M5 Ultra chips, signaling a rapid industry shift toward sub-3nm nodes for high-performance AI workloads.
The industry is increasingly moving toward custom, non-commercial silicon, as evidenced by OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip, which is being used to benchmark against established market rivals.

posts.title: Ferroelectric Tuning Reduces Optical-Interconnect Stalls In LLM Training (Georgia Tech)
posts.summary:
Researchers from Georgia Institute of Technology published a technical paper titled “Thermal Tuning Overhead in Wafer-Scale Optical Interconnects for LLM MoE Training: A Cross-Layer Analysis and Ferroelectric-Based Mitigation.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper analyzes “wafer-scale optical interconnects” for mixture-of-experts LLM training and finds “repeated tuning stalls during communication phases.” It also reports “speedups of 2.7x” for... » read more
The post Ferroelectric Tuning Reduces Optical-Interconnect Stalls In LLM Training (Georgia Tech) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Georgia Tech researchers identified that thermal tuning in wafer-scale optical interconnects causes significant communication stalls during LLM mixture-of-experts (MoE) training.
The study proposes a ferroelectric-based mitigation strategy to address these thermal overheads.
Implementing this solution resulted in a 2.7x speedup for Mixtral 8x7B training, highlighting a critical bottleneck for large-scale AI infrastructure.

posts.title: Generative Design Optimizes Liquid-Cooling Channels For 2.5D And 3D Packages (UM-Dearborn)
posts.summary:
Researchers from University of Michigan-Dearborn published a technical paper titled “Generative Design of Liquid-Cooling Channels for Thermal Management of 2.5D and 3D Integrated Advanced Packaging.” Abstract Excerpt: The paper presents “a physics-guided generative design framework for liquid cooling channel topology optimization” in a “2.7 kW multi-chip package containing two high power GPUs and one CPU.”... » read more
The post Generative Design Optimizes Liquid-Cooling Channels For 2.5D And 3D Packages (UM-Dearborn) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers at UM-Dearborn developed a physics-guided generative design framework to optimize liquid-cooling channel topology for high-power multi-chip packages.
Testing on a 2.7 kW package containing two GPUs and one CPU demonstrated a 33.6% reduction in maximum GPU temperature.
The design also achieved a 52.5% improvement in temperature uniformity and a 72.8% reduction in pressure drop, addressing key thermal management challenges in dense 3D integration.
